📝 Notes
Jan 30, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Amir Houieh updated the team on their website, now a Next.js project with an integrated blog, and introduced an initial sketch of an attention-based memory layer hobby project. Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes discussed the significant business opportunity of this memory tool for therapists, estimating it could save them 1.5 hours per day and be highly valued, which prompted a discussion about local deployment and security concerns with Noémi Biró. The main talking points included the website update, the introduction of the attention-based memory layer, its potential as a business tool for therapists, and considerations for local deployment, security, and hardware for the tool.
Details
Website and Hobby Project Updates Amir Houieh provided an update on the website, noting that it is now a proper Next.js project, not just a mockup, and includes an integrated blog generated from markdown files. Amir Houieh also introduced their hobby project, which is an initial sketch of an attention-based memory layer focused on topics that require attention, rather than storing all data, which Gabor Kerekes related to a conversation about therapists' challenges with attention splitting between listening and note-taking (00:01:41). They explained that this memory layer is "very purpose driven," and could be told what to focus on, such as user anger or development principles in logs (00:03:05).
Business Opportunity for Therapist Tool The conversation pivoted to the potential business value of the memory tool for therapists, as Amir Houieh stated that they confirmed with multiple therapists, including their own and a physiotherapist, that taking notes and writing reports after sessions takes about 15 minutes per one-hour session (00:04:25). Amir Houieh estimated that this system could save each therapist about 1.5 hours per day, which translates to a financial worth of several hundred Euros daily, suggesting they would easily pay for the service (00:05:24). Gabor Kerekes emphasized the high motivation from therapists, as they would even pay for such a system themself if their employer would not (00:04:25).
Security and Deployment Considerations Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes discussed security and deployment for a therapist-focused tool, noting that making the system local could address many security and privacy concerns, a key factor for therapists according to Noémi Biró. They considered the complexity of running a language model locally, which would require strong enough laptops (00:05:24) (00:07:54). Gabor Kerekes suggested shipping the hardware with the software, but Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró expressed doubt about the financial and sustainability viability of such a model, given that clinics might be small or have recently invested in new IT equipment (00:09:03). Gabor Kerekes acknowledged that they were getting ahead of themself, and they should first better define the system's needs before focusing on implementation details (00:10:55).
Next Steps for the Memory Layer Amir Houieh mentioned that they would have the initial version of the memory or "brain" ready by next week, and they want to set it up for the team to feed it with different data and jobs (00:06:44). Amir Houieh referenced Gabor Kerekes's idea of connecting it to cloud code to observe interactions over a week (00:07:54). Noémi Biró confirmed the plan for the following week to focus on setting up the memory layer on each other's devices (00:11:55). Amir Houieh also shared that both their therapist and Hoda have expressed willingness to try the system once it is ready (00:10:55).
Upcoming Moderating Sessions Noémi Biró informed the team about their upcoming moderating work, which involves introductions and Q&A sessions with film directors after screenings. They mentioned having eight sessions in total until Tuesday (00:11:55).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will have the initial version of the memory layer ready by next week.
The group will set up the memory layer on each other's devices next week to feed it with different data and assign different jobs.
